headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading error: kotaemon handles API keys and broad network egress while nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress, but the pairwise bridge is undocumented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: kotaemon exposes a web UI and file inputs, so prompt injection is plausible if nuwa-skill feeds it untrusted content; however, no shared channel or direct ingestion path is documented in either profile. The interaction is inferred, not observed, so I choose low rather than none because uncertainty must escalate.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill passes attacker-controlled text into kotaemon's web UI or file inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF the two agents are bridged by copy-paste or a shared workspace, the risk increases.
mitigations: Restrict pasted content to trusted sources only.
Add a manual review step before kotaemon processes nuwa-skill output.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Disable any auto-ingest or auto-run workflow between them.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on transferred content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon touches API keys and broad document classes, and its broad network egress can send content to third-party APIs. nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress, so if it receives kotaemon outputs or shares a workspace, sensitive material could leak in default use. The pairwise path is undocumented, but the data classes and egress surfaces make medium appropriate.
conditions: IF kotaemon processes documents containing API keys or chat transcripts and forwards them to external APIs, leakage occurs.
IF nuwa-skill reads kotaemon outputs from a shared workspace, sensitive data can propagate to its own egress path.
mitigations: Remove secrets from inputs before either agent sees them.
Use separate, access-controlled directories for each agent.
Block external API calls for sensitive jobs.
Review outbound destinations for both agents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-file data classification and egress policy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: kotaemon supports multiple instances and writes to ./ktem_app_data, while nuwa-skill has no documented write surface or concurrency model. A direct write-write conflict is not evidenced, so the overlap is limited and low severity. If nuwa-skill also writes to the same directory, the severity would rise.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill is configured to write into kotaemon's ./ktem_app_data directory, file contention can occur.
IF both agents are run concurrently against the same mutable resource, conflicts become possible.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Run only one writer at a time.
Make shared files read-only.
Check for lock files before writes.
requires-engineering: add explicit locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon is a RAG/chat system that can generate citations and answers, and nuwa-skill could plausibly consume those outputs as inputs. Because no verification or critique step is documented, an error in kotaemon can cascade into nuwa-skill actions or reports. The interaction is inferred, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill treats kotaemon output as authoritative, downstream errors can propagate.
IF kotaemon hallucinates or mis-cites and nuwa-skill reuses that content, the cascade persists.
mitigations: Require human review of kotaemon outputs before reuse.
Add a verification checklist in nuwa-skill.
Compare outputs against source documents.
Flag uncited claims for rejection.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon handles API keys and document/chat data, while nuwa-skill's residency and retention posture is undocumented. If the pair processes regulated or sensitive data, the mismatch in documented controls creates a compliance gap. I do not cite nuwa-skill-specific residency because none is stated; uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through kotaemon and then forwarded to nuwa-skill, compliance review is required.
IF either agent retains data longer than the other, retention mismatch becomes material.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair.
Document retention and deletion expectations.
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workflows.
Review vendor terms before deployment.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
